changes.local: In many common circumstances, including, for example, room temperature air, the gas particles have negligible volume and do not interact with each other, aside from perfectly elastic collisions. In such cases, the gas is called an ideal gas, in which case the relationship between the pressure, volume, and temperature is given by the equation of state called the ideal gas law.
